key_insight: Adding NiCr-Cr3C2 for load-bearing wear resistance and Ni-MoS2 for lubricating Mo/S species creates a synergistic Fe-based flame-sprayed coating with better tribological balance than either function alone.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical composition guideline for designing lower-cost thermally sprayed coatings that can simultaneously resist wear and reduce friction in sliding components.
method: Flame-sprayed Fe60-based coatings with varying NiCr-Cr3C2 and Ni-coated MoS2 contents.
Characterized phase constitution, microstructure, hardness, friction, wear rate, and worn surfaces using XRD, SEM/EDS, and cross-sectional wear-track profiling.
Compared nine formulations to identify the best tradeoff between friction reduction and wear resistance.
evidence_signal: The best-performing composition (C6: 15 wt.% Ni-MoS2 + 40 wt.% NiCr-Cr3C2) achieved the lowest friction coefficient (0.50), a wear rate of 0.59 × 10^-4 mm3/(N·m), and the highest microhardness.
watch_item: MoS2 is partially thermally transformed during spraying, so performance depends on controlling spray-induced phase changes and preserving useful Mo/S-containing products.
paper_title: Tribological Properties of Flame-Sprayed Fe-Based Composite Coatings Synergistically Enhanced by NiCr-Cr3C2 and Ni-MoS2
